transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

This symptom—stopping mid-cycle but resuming when the door is nudged—is classic for an intermittent door interlock issue. The microwave's safety system detects a momentary loss of contact and cuts power to prevent radiation leakage; reseating the door restores it. While a control board glitch is possible, the mechanical link is far more likely. Please check if there is any grease or debris in the door latch area that might be preventing a solid seal, and ensure the plastic hooks aren't cracked.

I've cleaned the grease from around the door hooks and latch slots, but it still happened once since. No smell, sparks or tripping, and the door looks very slightly lower on the handle side, though I can't be sure. What next?

We are looking at either a mechanical alignment issue or a worn interlock switch that isn't making solid contact when the door is under load. The next step is to check for physical play: with it unplugged, try to wiggle the door handle; if there's significant wobble, the hinges or latch mechanism may be misaligned. If the fit feels firm but it still stops, the internal microswitches are likely worn and need replacement by an engineer.

I can't get at the plug as it's screwed into the tall unit, and I won't pull it out. I'm not sure how much wobble counts as significant. The door does look very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't be certain. Would this need an engineer? It's out of Bosch's 2-year warranty, but I'd pay for a visit.

Yes, this will need an engineer. Because the microwave stops mid-cycle and only resumes when you physically move the door, it indicates that one of the internal safety microswitches is worn or misaligned and losing contact under vibration or heat. This requires a qualified technician to dismantle the unit, check the switch continuity, and replace the faulty component. Please book an engineer visit.
